key_insight: MLLM failures on fine-grained visual questions often come from a regional-to-global perception gap: models answer correctly when given evidence-centered crops but fail on full images. Training with on-policy self-distillation teaches the model to transfer crop-level attention to whole-image reasoning, improving fine-detail perception.
problem_solved: Reduces missed or incorrect answers caused by inability to focus on small but decisive visual evidence in full images, improving fine-grained visual understanding for multimodal LLMs.
method: Identify evidence-centered crops that lead to correct answers and use them as teacher signals for the full-image student model (on-policy self-distillation).
Train the MLLM to align attention and predictions between crop-conditioned and full-image-conditioned inputs so the model learns to focus on small, decisive regions in context.
Iteratively refine the model by generating its own crop-conditioned supervision during training (on-policy loop) to scale fine-detail supervision without manual annotations.
impact: Enables MLLMs to reliably use small, critical visual cues in real-world tasks (e.g., visual QA, instruction following, inspection), boosting accuracy and robustness without requiring dense pixel-level labels.
visual_elements: Side-by-side example: full image vs evidence-centered crop with model answers (correct on crop, wrong on full) to illustrate the perception gap.
Pipeline diagram of on-policy self-distillation: crop selection → teacher prediction → student full-image training → iterative loop.
Attention/heatmap overlay sequence showing how the model's focus shifts from diffuse to targeted regions after distillation.
Bar/line chart comparing baseline vs Vision-OPD performance on fine-grained benchmarks (accuracy gains) and sample-efficiency of training.
paper_title: Vision-OPD: Learning to See Fine Details for Multimodal LLMs via On-Policy Self-Distillation
paper_authors: Qianhao Yuan, Jie Lou, Xing Yu, Hongyu Lin, Le Sun
